rv.q: A singular projection reminds us that it is indeed 1879. In some ways, it feels disappointing to lose the visual fullness of Ibsen’s world. Despite it being Christmastime in the Helmer house, a plentiful one at that, staples such as presents or sweets are discussed but never shown.

At best the production presents an interesting exercise in remoulding a classic, but many hours after attending opening night, I am still wondering whether I liked what I saw, or whether am I merely unsettled by the incongruities inherent in its determination to appear current.
